title: Rambam on Mishnah Kelim
text: He placed sand between one ring-section and another, so that he would make a ring-section and then place sand around it, and fit a second ring-section onto that sand — and he continued doing this until he completed the shape of the oven. He then plastered it on the outside with clay until he finished it. Rabbi Eliezer said that the sand separates between the ring-sections, and therefore it is as if it were broken and divided permanently — and for this reason it is ritually pure. But the Sages say that the clay touching all the ring-sections on the outside has already joined them together and made that oven whole. A great and weighty dispute fell between Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages, with many proofs brought on both sides, until on that very day Rabban Gamliel and his court burned all the pure things that Rabbi Eliezer had declared pure, and they excommunicated him. For this reason it is called the Oven of Akhnai attributed to akhnah, which is a large serpent. They said that the responses [arguments] surrounded it like a serpent. Similarly, many matters arose concerning the earthen pits of the Arabs — that is, the pit dug in the ground for baking and afterwards assemblies convened and agreed upon the ruling mentioned here. For this reason this form is called the Oven of Ben Dinai, attributed to din. The law does not follow Rabbi Eliezer.
